countries.vegetation: Extensive pine plantations, birch, flat glacial plains, lakes in the north.
countries.cars: Large western second-hand fleet, heavy on VW, Opel and Škoda.

countries.name: Ukraine
tells: Ukrainian Cyrillic exclusives І, Ї, Є and Ґ — none of which exist in Russian, Bulgarian, Serbian or Macedonian.
Street abbreviation is вул. (not ул.), and a city is prefixed м. rather than Russian г.
Company names carry ТОВ or ФОП, not Russian ООО.
Licence plates are white with a blue-over-yellow band on the left — Russia's are plain white with the flag at the right end.
Square-section concrete utility poles, often with a diagonal brace or a wooden pole strapped to a concrete stub.
Guardrails, kerbs and tree trunks painted in black-and-white bands.
Pedestrian crossing sign drawn with three stripes.
Vast flat black-earth farmland with sunflower and wheat; birch and poplar shelter belts.
countries.plate: White plate with a blue-over-yellow national band on the left reading UA. Two letters, four digits, two letters.
countries.script: Cyrillic (Ukrainian). І, Ї, Є, Ґ present; Ы, Э, Ё absent; Ъ is not used, an apostrophe takes its place.
countries.roadLines: White, frequently worn.
countries.bollard: Varied and inconsistent; the Polish wraparound style appears in Zakarpattia in the far west.
countries.poles: Square concrete poles with varying tops, sometimes whitewashed at the base; diagonal braces common.
countries.signs: White town entry signs. Red chevrons with white arrows. Black-and-white painted guardrails.
countries.chevrons: White arrows on red.
countries.guardrail: Steel barriers, very often painted in black-and-white bands.
countries.architecture: Light grey brick Soviet-era apartment blocks; single-family brick houses with corrugated roofs behind fences in the suburbs; Hungarian-influenced forms near the western border.
countries.vegetation: Flat black-earth steppe and farmland with sunflower and wheat; birch and poplar shelter belts; forest in the north and west; Carpathians in the far west.
countries.cars: Mixed: old Ladas and Soviet vehicles alongside imported European second-hand cars.

countries.name: Russia
tells: Russian Cyrillic has Ы, Э and Ё — none of which exist in Bulgarian, Ukrainian, Serbian or Macedonian. Ы in particular turns up constantly.
Ъ appears only as a rare hard sign, never as a vowel and never at the start of a word — the opposite of Bulgarian usage.
Company names carry ООО, ЗАО or ИП.
Licence plates are plain white with the flag and RUS at the RIGHT-hand end, with no blue band on the left.
Guardrails, kerbs and tree trunks painted in black-and-white bands.
Birch and spruce forest over enormous distances; concrete slab roads in the far north.
Right-hand-drive Japanese imports become increasingly common east of roughly Novosibirsk.
Bilingual town signs in the minority-language republics such as Tatarstan and Bashkortostan.
countries.plate: White plate, black characters, with the Russian flag and RUS at the right-hand end and a small regional code. No EU-style blue band on the left.
countries.script: Cyrillic (Russian). Ы, Э, Ё present; no І, Ї, Є, Ґ, Љ, Њ, Џ, Ј.
countries.roadLines: White; yellow has been permitted as an alternative for separating opposing traffic in recent years but remains uncommon.
countries.bollard: Varies enormously by region; a thin post mounted on a stick is typical of the east, from roughly Omsk onwards.
countries.poles: Mostly concrete, square or round depending on region; wooden poles in the north and Siberia.
countries.signs: Warning triangles white with a red border. Regional quirks: black-bottomed signs around Stavropol, Chechnya and western Dagestan.
countries.chevrons: White arrows on red.
countries.guardrail: Steel barriers, commonly painted in black-and-white bands; concrete slab roadways in the far north.
countries.architecture: Soviet panel blocks in every city; wooden houses in the north and Siberia; red brick in the south; white limestone in Dagestan.
countries.vegetation: Birch and spruce taiga across most of the country; steppe in the south; tundra in the far north.
countries.cars: Lada in enormous numbers, plus UAZ and GAZ; Japanese right-hand-drive imports in the east.

countries.name: Moldova
tells: Romanian language in Latin script — Ă, Â, Î, Ș, Ț — combined with post-Soviet infrastructure, which is the combination that names the country.
Licence plates are white with a WIDER-than-standard blue band carrying the Moldovan tricolour over MD; the format is three letters and three digits.
Guardrails, kerbs and tree trunks painted in black-and-white bands, as in Ukraine.
Rolling farmland, vineyards and walnut trees; almost no mountains.
Very old vehicle fleet — Ladas alongside Dacias and western second-hand imports.
Russian-language signage appears alongside Romanian, especially in the north and in Transnistria.
countries.plate: White plate with a wider blue band on the left carrying the Moldovan flag over MD; three letters and three digits in embossed FE-Schrift lettering.
countries.script: Latin (Romanian), with Russian Cyrillic alongside it in places.
countries.roadLines: White, often worn; road quality is poor away from main corridors.
countries.bollard: Not well documented — do not rely on it here.
countries.poles: Concrete poles in post-Soviet styles, similar to Ukraine's.
countries.signs: Warning triangles white with a red border; Romanian-language text, sometimes with Russian.
countries.chevrons: Not reliably documented.
countries.guardrail: Steel barriers, often painted in black-and-white bands.
countries.architecture: Single-storey rural houses with painted plaster and decorative gates; Soviet panel blocks in Chișinău and the larger towns.
countries.vegetation: Rolling farmland, vineyards on a large scale, walnut and acacia along the roads; no significant mountains.
countries.cars: Very old fleet: Lada, Dacia and western second-hand imports.

countries.name: Italy
tells: Licence plates with blue bands on BOTH sides, and a front plate noticeably shorter than the rear.
Triangular bollards, white with a black cap, red reflector front and white rear — identical to Albania's, so check the plate.
Round concrete poles with a concrete TRIDENT top; round concrete poles are themselves uncommon around the Mediterranean.
Solid white outer lines with no centre line on many rural roads.
The backs of road signs are black or dark grey.
Chevrons are white arrows on a black board.
Direction signs are blue with white arrows and set in all capitals; street signs are white with a thin blue border and black text.
Pastel stone houses with terracotta roofs and wooden shutters split in two that open sideways.
Fiat Panda, Punto and 500 as the default small car; heavy scooter use.
countries.plate: White EU plate with blue bands on BOTH the left and right. Two letters, three digits, two letters. The front plate is shorter than the rear.
countries.script: Latin (Italian). Accented vowels à, è, ì, ò, ù; no unusual letters.
countries.roadLines: White; solid outer lines with no centre line is a characteristic rural layout, shared with Czechia.
countries.bollard: Triangular in plan, white with a black top, red front reflector and white rear.
countries.poles: Round concrete poles with concrete trident tops; wooden poles carry a small white sticker.
countries.signs: Warning triangles white with a red border. Blue direction signs with white all-caps text. Sign backs black or dark grey.
countries.chevrons: White arrows on black.
countries.guardrail: Standard steel barriers.
countries.architecture: Pastel stone houses with terracotta roofs, two-part wooden shutters opening sideways, narrow historic streets.
countries.vegetation: Alpine in the north; Po plain farmland; Mediterranean olive, cypress and pine through the centre and south.
countries.cars: Fiat dominates in small cars; very heavy scooter and small-van traffic.
countries.phone: +39 — landlines keep the leading 0 even with the country code

countries.name: Spain
tells: Spanish Latin script with Ñ and inverted opening punctuation ¿ and ¡.
Bollards are white with GREY reflectors on both sides — grey reflectors are unusual in Europe.
Kilometre markers are colour-coded by road class: orange, green then yellow borders from largest to smallest roads.
Heavy regional variation in bollards, markers and signage — Catalonia, Andalusia, the Basque provinces and Murcia all differ visibly.
Chevrons vary by region: large square boards with a single arrow in Catalonia, small square red-on-white boards in Murcia.
Bilingual signage in Catalonia, Valencia, the Basque Country and Galicia.
Dry pale interior plateaus with olive and almond groves; white-walled villages in the south.
countries.plate: White EU plate with a blue band reading E. Four digits followed by three letters, with no regional code since 2000.
countries.script: Latin (Spanish), plus Catalan, Basque and Galician on regional signage.
countries.roadLines: White; edge-line style varies noticeably between provinces, which is itself a regional clue.
countries.bollard: White body with grey reflectors on both sides; regional variants include green tops in Extremadura and an orange front reflector in Lleida and Tarragona.
countries.poles: Varied; steel mesh poles forming rectangular shapes are characteristic of Murcia and southern Alicante.
countries.signs: Warning triangles white with a red border. Kilometre markers colour-coded by road class; Andalusian markers are unusually tall.
countries.chevrons: Regionally variable — square boards with red or black arrows.
countries.guardrail: Standard steel barriers; Ceuta uses black-and-white painted rails.
countries.architecture: White-walled villages with terracotta roofs in the south; stone and brick in the north; large modern apartment blocks along the coast.
countries.vegetation: Dry pale interior plateau with olive and almond groves and holm oak; green Atlantic north; palm and citrus along the Mediterranean coast.
countries.cars: Seat is the domestic marque and very common; otherwise a standard western European fleet.
